correctness.rationale: Reconstructing the disease-free infected subsystem gives K with characteristic polynomial z^2-a z-c. Neither threshold depends on lambda_h; both a and c decrease in delta_h and gamma_h, so their sensitivities are strictly negative. Fresh exact arithmetic reproduced the source-parameter threshold 1.3188521516976628 and elasticities -0.7532247434 and -0.2353827323 for delta_h and gamma_h.
risks: No claim is made about fractional-order stability regions away from invasion threshold.

source_inspections.title: Existence theory and numerical solution of leptospirosis disease model via exponential decay law
source_inspections.trigger: Exact source whose sensitivity conclusions are corrected.

evidence: Direct human transmission dominates the source parameter set; recovery/removal signs are reversed relative to the published interpretation.
value.rationale: The corrected signs reverse the interpretation of recovery and disease-induced removal and make loss of immunity exactly irrelevant to invasion. Because the source explicitly uses sensitivity analysis to prioritize epidemic controls, this is a substantive correction despite the short derivative calculation.
risks: The mathematical sign of disease-induced mortality is not a public-health recommendation.

final_claim: For the printed host-vector leptospirosis model, loss of immunity has zero invasion-threshold sensitivity while human recovery and disease-induced mortality have strictly negative sensitivity, under both the standard next-generation spectral radius and the threshold-equivalent direct-plus-vector normalization.
limitations: No correction of all numerical trajectories or fractional stability claims.
